newsitem.title: USA: Pacific Intertie spring plan review begins Mar 20.
newsitem.headline: Pacific Intertie spring plan review begins Mar 20.

text.p: The board of the Western Systems Coordinating Council (WSCC) will begin formal review of spring operations for the Pacific Intertie on March 20, if a timeframe agreed to Thursday is met, a Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) spokeswoman said Friday.
As a result, there is a reasonable chance of the "spring" plan being cleared for implementation ahead of the expiration of winter operating criteria, spokeswoman Cheri Larsen noted.
A spokeswoman for the WSCC agreed the spring plan could be approved ahead of the runoff season, but it will be close.
"It all depends on the comments," she noted.
The WSCC and BPA previously expressed concerns of a gap between the two plans.
BPA concluded a meeting with a WSCC study group on Thursday, when studies supporting raising the interstate transmission system capacity to 7,800 MW were presented, Larsen said.

The WSCC study group is next scheduled to convene March 18, when it is expected to formalize a spring operating plan, which would be passed on to the WSCC board for formal review as early as March 20.
The review process would take about 30 days.
A "winter" operating plan for the intertie lines is currently undergoing a similar review, with a final decision expected later this month.
The winter plan would raise capacity to 6,250 MW, but would remain in effect only until late April, when spring operating conditions would alter use of the transmission system.
If the spring plan is not fully approved by the time the winter criteria expires, use of the intertie lines would revert back to 5,200 MW.
But if all goes smoothly, the two plans would dovetail, with little or no gap between them
